sources_considered.why: Direct prepublication study of internal, updating representations in pretrained natural-language models; includes interventions and explicit reliability limitations.
Prepublication evidence of successful state tracking, but in transformers trained on chess notation rather than ordinary natural language.
Examined as a candidate counterexample. Its separate symbolic world model prevents attributing the complete maintained model to the LLM itself.

evidence_items.locator: Section 6, Conclusion; reliability qualifications in Section 5

receipt.public_excerpt: These internal representations are structured, interpretably localized, and editable.

evidence_items.explanation: Li, Nye, and Andreas demonstrate state representations and interventions in BART and T5, which challenges a simple absence claim. Their limitations section reports complete-state recovery of only 53.8% even in the best case and leaves richer situations untested, so reliable functional use remains unsettled.

receipt.public_excerpt: Unlike natural language, chess notations describe a simple, constrained, and deterministic domain.

evidence_items.explanation: The authors report accurate piece tracking and legal-move prediction from move sequences. This is relevant evidence of functional state tracking, but the specialized chess setting does not establish reliable cognitive-model use by the natural-language LLMs discussed in the post.

unresolved_gaps: The located studies do not establish reliable downstream use of the relevant representations under a clearly matching interpretation of the claim.
The search does not establish the universal absence of an earlier qualifying demonstration.
The speaker supplies no reliability threshold that resolves the borderline demonstrations.
